useCase.name: Take a report away in print or as a file, carrying exactly what was on screen and nothing further

intent.name: report.export
intent.summary: Take a report you have run away as a file — a spreadsheet for a list, a PDF for anything — carrying exactly what was on screen and nothing further. Every export is recorded.

routesHere.gloss: give it to me as a PDF

routesHere: download this report as a spreadsheet

routesHere.gloss: I need the receipt register in excel

routesHere.text: jo report abhi chalayi uski file bana do
routesHere.gloss: make a file of the report I just ran

routesElsewhere.note: Any report may be printed (BR-1), but printing happens on the reader's own device. A plan hands back a PDF, which prints the same way.

request.text: salary column bhi export mein daal do
request.gloss: put the salary column in the export too

routesElsewhere.note: An export carries exactly the rows and columns the reader could see on screen and nothing further — the salary rule applies to the file as to the screen (BR-2, E1).

request.text: mujhe download ki permission de do

routesElsewhere.note: Downloading is not a permission of its own. Whoever may read a report may take it away (BR-4, E8).

request.text: har mahine khud ba khud bhej diya kare

routesElsewhere.note: Scheduling a report to be produced and sent is not modelled.

request.text: kis ne kaun si report export ki?

routesElsewhere.note: Every export is written to the audit log (BR-3).

steps.note: One step. The file is built from the result the reader saw, never from the underlying query (BR-2), and the export is recorded (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A spreadsheet for a report that is not a list is refused, and an export that cannot be recorded is not produced.
plan.atomicity: The file and its audit entry together, or neither — an export that cannot be recorded does not complete (BR-3, E4). No record is changed.

operations.name: report.export
operations.purpose: Produce a file from a report result, carrying exactly what was shown.

parameters.name: result_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No report this reader has run matches — a report is exported from its result, so it is run first.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the reader's recent report runs with their parameters.

parameters.notes: The report as the reader ran it — its rows, its columns, its parameters (BR-2). Usually the one just run.

parameters.name: format
parameters.notes: A spreadsheet for a list somebody will filter and sort; a PDF for anything signed, filed or sent unaltered (BR-1). Print is done from the screen.

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The reader. Every run is recorded against them. Never from the request.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: rows_exported
fields.description: How many rows left the system — recorded on the audit entry (BR-3).

fields.name: columns_omitted
fields.description: Columns withheld because the reader could not see them on screen — the salary section among them (BR-2).

fields.name: header
fields.description: The school and branch, the report, its parameters, the date and time, and the user — on every file (BR-5).

fields.name: in_parts
fields.description: True where the result was too large for one file and was produced in parts (E9).

errors.meaning: A spreadsheet was asked for a report that is not a list.
The export could not be written to the audit log.
errors.note: A file that leaves unrecorded is not seen again (BR-3).

errors.meaning: The result was too large for one file.
errors.written: The files and the audit entry.
errors.note: Produced in parts rather than truncated silently.

operations.writesOnRead: An audit entry: the user, the report, its parameters, the format and the row count (BR-3). The file leaves the system and is not seen again.

planningRules.rule: Export only what the reader saw. The file carries exactly the rows and columns shown on screen — never the underlying query, which would return restricted columns (BR-2, A2, AC-5).
Never add a column the reader could not see, and never a row from another branch. A salary the reader may not see stays out of the file as it stayed off the screen (BR-2, E1, E2, A1, AC-4, AC-9).

Never ask for or grant a download permission. There is none — whoever may read a report may take it away, and what limits exposure is who may open the report and the field restrictions (BR-4, A5, E8, AC-1).
Offer a spreadsheet only for a list. Anything else goes as a PDF (BR-1, A3, E3, AC-2, AC-3).
Say that the export is recorded — the user, the report, its parameters, the format and the row count — and that an export that cannot be recorded is not produced (BR-3, E4, AC-6, AC-7).
Where the file holds guardians' numbers or identity numbers — the student directory above all — say what is leaving. Nothing refuses a large export; it is only recorded (BR-3, OQ-2).
staff_id and branch_id come from $session. A file never crosses into a branch the reader cannot open (BR-6).

reversal.statement: Nothing is written to any record. The file exists once produced, and the audit entry stands (BR-3).

request.text: jo receipt register abhi chalaya uska excel bana do

intent.name: report.combined.run
intent.summary: Run a report across all branches at once, as one combined set of figures. The Super Admin alone — nobody else can run it, open it or be given it.
routesHere: run the collection summary across all campuses for October

routesHere.text: saari branches ka combined trial balance nikaalo
routesHere.gloss: pull out the combined trial balance of all branches

routesHere.text: poore group ka outstanding ek report mein
routesHere.gloss: the whole group's outstanding in one report

routesHere: combined income and expenditure for the year

request.text: Principal ko combined report ka access de do
request.gloss: give the Principal access to the combined report

routesElsewhere.note: A combined report cannot be granted to anybody (BR-9, E7). The branch use case lets the Super Admin grant a consolidated view (branch.consolidatedview.grant, UC-23-01); for reports this use case says no, and the two are unreconciled (OQ-1).

request.text: main Principal hoon, saari branches ki report chahiye
request.gloss: I am the Principal, I need the report of all branches

routesElsewhere.note: A Principal asks the Super Admin for the figure; they cannot produce it themselves (BR-9, A4, E6).

request.text: Model Town branch ki report alag se
request.gloss: Model Town branch's report on its own

routesElsewhere.goesTo: The branch's own report, after switching branch in the header.
routesElsewhere.note: The Super Admin also reads each branch on its own (BR-7, A6).

steps.note: One step. One set of figures for the whole group, offered to nobody else (BR-8, BR-9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Anybody but the Super Admin is refused.
plan.atomicity: A read. It changes nothing; the run is recorded as every report run is.

operations.name: report.combined.run
operations.purpose: Run a catalogue report across all branches as one combined set of figures.

parameters.name: report_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No report in the catalogue matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the matching reports with their groups.

parameters.notes: Any report in the catalogue (BR-8). It matters most for finance: collection, the cash book, outstanding and defaulters, invoices and receipts, concessions and write-offs, the general ledger, the trial balance, income and expenditure, and budget against actual.

parameters.name: parameters
parameters.notes: The period and scope the report takes when run for one branch — never a branch, since it covers them all.

fields.name: result_id
fields.description: The run. It is taken away with report.export.

fields.name: branches_covered
fields.description: Every branch whose figures are in it.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: One set of figures for the whole group (BR-8).

errors.meaning: Somebody other than the Super Admin tried to run it.
errors.note: A Principal or School Admin asks the Super Admin for the figure (BR-9, A4).

operations.writesOnRead: The run is recorded, as every report run is — the reports' own use cases say so; this one does not restate it.

planningRules.rule: The Super Admin alone. A Principal or School Admin asking is refused and told to ask the Super Admin — they cannot produce a group figure or be granted the right to (BR-9, A4, E6, AC-10).
Never offer to grant it. There is no such control (BR-9, E7, AC-11).
Say that it is one set of figures for the group, not branch reports added up by hand (BR-8, AC-12).
Say that the specification points the other way elsewhere — the branch use case lets the Super Admin grant a consolidated view, and this use case forbids it for reports (OQ-1).
Take it away through report.export, like any report (BR-10).

reversal.statement: A report changes nothing a plan can take back. The record of the run stands.

request.text: saari branches ka October ka collection summary ek report mein
request.gloss: October's collection summary for all branches in one report

resolvedPlans.outcome: One collection summary for the whole group for October, with every branch it covers named.

request.text: main Principal hoon, saari branches ka outstanding chahiye
request.gloss: I'm the Principal, I need outstanding for all branches

resolvedPlans.outcome: Refused — a report across branches is run by the Super Admin alone, and cannot be given to anybody. They can ask the Super Admin for the figure, or run their own branch's report.
